[2024-10-01 00:35] fatherborf : yeah comments are really good indicators but dont seem to work at all as necessarily accurate "limits" except for negative comments - for example i have a PG with "above average post moves" who is a RS SR, and maybe i get lucky and it pops a bunch now, but he only has 9 IS - for Bates my PG does not have a "long range shooter" comment, but has 18 range. and his only defensive comment is "Will never be a good interior defender." - and thats true, he only has 2 ID... but he has 18 PD. So comments like "Can be a decent rebounder" dont *guarantee* they will end up with precisely like 14-16 rebounding.
[2024-10-01 00:43] fatherborf : to simplify it as a broad concept to apply: if you are choosing between two similar recruits and one has a negative comment in a skill you value a lot, and the other has no comment at all, no comment is usually better. For someone with "Does not have much of a shooting touch" it is, as far as i know, impossible for them to have like 16 OS. I dont even think Ive had anyone who had a negative comment and were starting college at 5 or less in the skill, ever hit double digits in said skill, but ive not played nearly as long as a lot of these guys so there may be really notable exceptions. Some of my best players so far have kinda consistently been dudes who simply had like only 2 or 3 positive comments and zero bad ones and developed into players just as talented as any of my "good/excellent all around player" comment recruits

[2024-10-05 21:27] fatherborf : This is extremely preliminary and I have a lot more to collect, and it will take a while cuz im controlling for as many variables as i *reasonably* can, and then looking at it from several different perspectives, but here is some very early data on player dev in relation to HS dev and potential, that mostly confirms what was already suspected
[2024-10-05 21:31] fatherborf : BC, to me, it is unclear **exactly** how RS works (how important is 0 games vs 5 games, since it works "retroactively" at the flip, does it have an effect on their Dev #0 update for the season following RS? etc)  i simply removed any RS seasons/data - this is also mostly 11 and 12 potential players, with a few 9+10s and 13s, as they seem to be the most common and 13+ potential seems to often get drafted, which makes it hard to know retrospectively what SI they were at graduation)
[2024-10-05 21:35] fatherborf : but HS dev is an extremely good indicator of 4-season college development. the average difference so far between HS dev and 4 year college dev **total** is only 2.12 points. ~70% of the time a player will have between 8 less and 12 more points of dev over 4 years compared to their HS dev edit: updated with bigger sample size
[2024-10-05 21:38] fatherborf : but i think HS dev is more of an indicator, whereas potential is the main "driver" - average ratio of total dev per season to potential is 1.06, and again ~70% of the time a player is going to develop at a rate of 0.90-1.25 times their potential per season
[2024-10-05 21:47] fatherborf : and so far when players deviate significantly from these ranges it **seems** to usually be driven by starting closer or farther from the theoretical "skill cap" of a given potential rating.  so for example, on average youd expect an 11 pot to dev about 11.66 per season and a 12 pot to dev 12.72, but an 11 pot entering college at 121 SI is more likely to develop at a noticeably lower avg rate than 11.66, and a 12 pot entering college at only 80 SI will be more likely to grow at a noticeably faster rate than 12.7 per season, all things being equal
[2024-10-05 22:00] lassoball : This is great work, thanks for sharing
[2024-10-06 01:33] fatherborf : alright im up to a couple hundred now, and for more specific examples, basically if youre looking at a recruit with 11-12 potential, if they developed:  35 in HS, ~95% of the time theyll end up with 25-50 dev "pre-redshirt" in college, ~70% chance it ends up within 31-43 45 in HS, ~95% of the time theyll end up with 32-64 dev "pre-redshirt" in college, ~70% chance it ends up within 40-56 55 in HS, ~95% of the time theyll end up with 39-79 dev "pre-redshirt" in college, ~70% chance it ends up within 49-68
[2024-10-06 02:01] fatherborf : median HS dev is 1.06xPot and median college dev is 1.08xPot, so that could be viewed as validation of the theory that coaching skills probably have an effect but its very very very small
[2024-10-06 17:22] naph7777 : So what you're saying is expect +Pot each year... and more often than not you'll be pleasantly surprised, but not a lot more often.
[2024-10-06 21:34] fatherborf : yup - mostly just confirmed a lot of the things many had suspected but hadnt necessarily "tracked" - basically Pot is the main driver, and HS dev gives you a surprisingly accurate preview in most cases - more often than not, youll get at least Pot-Per-Year, and then whatever you get during the RS season. as with anything in hardwood, there are no guarantees.
[2024-10-06 21:37] fatherborf : one really funny thing i saw that i think is just a selection bias - i only had like 9 13 pot players out of the 220 i have recorded, and they are almost universally dogshit dev. worse average than 11
[2024-10-06 21:38] fatherborf : but its not that 13 dev actually sucks, its that most 13 dev athletes who are starting a lot of games end up making the pros, and i did not include any pro dev, so i only got to see the lowest developing 13 pots
[2024-10-06 21:41] fatherborf : so thats i guess another disclaimer - i am extremely extremely confident in the accuracy of what ive found for 11-12 pot, and i think it consistently applies to 9 and 10 pot too. i would **assume** the trends continue similarly at higher potential, but i dont actually have any idea. theoretically if everything stays consistent one hundred 14 pot guys should dev an avg of 14.5-15.0 per season, but i dont actually know if everything stays consistent or if stuff gets weird as your reach the upper limits of potential and SI

[2024-10-07 00:41] fatherborf : i didnt specifically record it but i did notice it when entering the data. no hard numbers but from what i saw yes in general FR and SO dev more than JR and SR, but there are of course some exceptions
[2024-10-07 00:42] fatherborf : the "chaos factor" steve introduced a little while ago that makes development less smooth but largely lead to the same totals makes that a little less predictable
[2024-10-07 00:44] fatherborf : if theyre gonna dev 50pts in 4 years it would **probably** look something like 17->14->10->9, but with that little chaos factor it can also kinda easily go 14->10->17->9
[2024-10-07 00:45] fatherborf : my next project is to try to look deeper into games/minutes/starter vs bench impact, but its something steve has done a really good job obfuscating
[2024-10-07 01:03] fatherborf : main problem ive run into so far is how RS confounds everything
[2024-10-07 01:04] fatherborf : despite the fact that there isnt much variability in HS games played since they have a hard ceiling of 120 games, and that like 84% of the players are playing 30-43 games per season, the trend is intriguing
[2024-10-07 01:05] fatherborf : the R^2 for HS games vs HS dev is 0.79, and for CO games vs CO dev its 0.75... but thats while not including RS seasons
[2024-10-07 01:06] fatherborf : when you add 100 seasons of 0-5 games and <200 minutes of play time resulting in nearly the same average dev as a non RS season, it fucks that all up
[2024-10-07 01:10] fatherborf : the logical problem we run into is that RS is only applied at the end of the season - when you check the box doesnt matter as long as its before the flip, which suggests there is no active system adjusting the development of RS players during the season, because many of them dont have the box checked until the end. this suggests that the RS players are simply developing at a "normal" rate - obviously games and minutes must have an impact, because RS is not nearly as consistently good as non RS dev, but the fact players can hit double digit development at all without any "adjustments" to their dev rate suggests that playtime, while still a big factor, is a much smaller factor than we had realized

[2024-10-07 01:18] fatherborf : a hard thing with minutes also becomes: if minutes have a large impact, doesnt that functionally mean stamina works as a secondary "potential" rating? [2024-10-17 04:53] fatherborf : basically yeah, potential is the "main" factor, but the displayed potential has decimals and isnt perfectly accurate, so HS dev is a pretty accurate indicator of expected 4 year growth. if you have two 12pot 100 SI players and one developed 40 and the other 60 in HS, the one with 60 will **probably** develop more, all else being equal. and of course because its sports and some randomness is fun, there are still outliers
[2024-10-17 04:55] fatherborf : thing to remember also is that steve changed the development rates a little while ago, so total dev is mostly the same but its less evenly distributed, so youre going to *generally* see more dev FR and SO year than SR
[2024-10-17 05:00] fatherborf : but yeah ~70% of the time over a 4 year span a player will gain between 1.2 less and 2.9 more per year than their displayed potential rating, and for HS dev ~70% of the time youd expect between ~85% and ~125% of HS dev. but then youd want to add RS growth on, and theres still about a 5% chance they end up growing 150% or more of their HS dev, and ~5% chance they only grow 40-60% as much.
[2024-10-17 05:04] fatherborf : once you have the players, the big thing to maximize their dev definitely seems to be getting them into games. the R^2 between total games played in college and total dev in college was 0.75
[2024-10-17 05:06] fatherborf : so even if a player has good pot and developed like 70 in HS, if they head into their RS SR season with only like 30 games under their belt, i would not expect them to have developed at the same rate

[2024-10-21 23:16] fatherborf : i was gonna answer that but realize i have a question of my own regarding that that i should have asked ages ago: i was operating under the assumption that I/i/~/o/O in game management effects where the players **position** themselves (generally) when they set up the offense, but does it also impact their preference for which shots to take? i had always assumed yes, like an O SG will both position outside the arc and prefer to take 3s than other shots
[2024-10-21 23:22] naph7777 : You've got a heap of PG/SG/SF options. But with the big options you have its probably going to be a development season. So if in doubt I'd probably go with the younger options at the guard positions.   Maybe:  Fabris - Templeton - Carroll - Breaux - Hickman
[2024-10-22 00:01] rlawrenceune : however, your team will adjust during the game based on success.  I've had plenty of games that I selected 'O" .. only to be surprised at how much inside shooting we did instead
[2024-10-22 03:11] naph7777 : Default positioning for players will have the guards on the perimeter more often and your bigs on the inside more often. Even a guard set on "I" is probably more often on the perimeter than a C set to "O". So you can also think of it like: "O" - run my offense through my guards a lot  "o" - run a bit more of the offense more through my guards. "~" - give equal opportunity to all players "i" - run a bit more offense through my bigs "I" - throw it in to the bigs a lot  Of course your individual game management settings also play a factor. Even  if you're on "I" as a team focus, if you're running +5 temp and have a PG set to O positioning and ++ green light.... don't be surprised if he's still jacking up a lot of 3's.
[2024-10-22 03:25] fatherborf : yeah this was basically my understanding of it so far; though in immediate retrospect idk why i was momentarily unsure when its in the names, offensive positioning and offensive emphasis 😅

[2024-10-30 03:08] fangraphs : And how does recruiting work?? I've fiddled around the menus a little bit but haven't found much success other than offering one guy lol
[2024-10-30 03:09] naph7777 : You spend recruiting contacts on players to increase their interest.  Players in region, particularly in state, might take 2-5 contacts to reach low interest... sometimes more (but that's generally an indication you should find someone else)
[2024-10-30 03:09] naph7777 : Players with any contacts, and a scholarship offer could sign with you. Only HS seniors, JuCo Sophomores and International players commit to a team... there is no commitments from HS juniors, sophomores etc.
[2024-10-30 03:10] naph7777 : Generally on players you actually want you will need to get to at least Medium, and probably High interest.

[2024-10-30 03:11] naph7777 : You get 2 per day... so I'd probably build back up to 20-30 before I spent more.
[2024-10-30 03:12] naph7777 : The interest levels are: Low, Low+, Low++, Medium, Medium+, Medium++, High, High+, High++, Very High  Though when you look at other team's recruiting boards you will only see Low/Medium/High (ie you see the "level" but not the "sub-level" of interest for other teams)

[2024-11-05 15:15] wooden47 : Potential determines skill caps, correct? Trying to wrap my head around what determines “dev rate”. Has there ever been a 13+ potential player that developed super slow?
[2024-11-05 16:16] wooden47 : Essentially my question boils down to: is dev rate a hidden stat or completely dependent on playing time.
[2024-11-05 16:44] cdilks : I wouldn't say 'hidden' so much as that the number we see isn't as exact or precise as what the game is using. The manual says a player's true skill can deviate by up to 20% from what is shown. The game also only shows whole numbers, but appears to use some sort of decimal on skills since some people have noticed the player search function rounding up skills on some searches.
[2024-11-05 16:50] cdilks : So theoretically a player with 13 POT could actually be more like an 11 in a worst case, or 15 in a best case--though I would guess those extremes are fairly rare. Watching a player's development rate in HS can give some clues about where within that range a player falls.
[2024-11-05 16:51] cdilks : I also tend to believe that playing time has a bigger impact.
[2024-11-05 16:54] naph7777 : http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/98290 - 13 Pot Dev: 10 - 8 - 11 - 10 - 10  Playing time certainly a factor.
[2024-11-05 16:56] naph7777 : http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/140552 - 13 pot Only 6 dev as a starting senior (30+mins/game) to graduate at 167 SI. Decent dev before then, but very good chance he was actually less than 13 pot.
[2024-11-05 17:07] wooden47 : Oh interesting
[2024-11-05 17:07] wooden47 : Did not realize there was a margin of variability on shown ratings vs actual ratings
[2024-11-05 17:08] wooden47 : Does this just apply to potential or does it apply to all ratings?
[2024-11-05 17:08] wooden47 : Like could a 15 ball handling actually be a 12 ball handling?
[2024-11-05 17:09] naph7777 : "- Scouted Skill Values vs. Real Skill Values So are the skill values displayed for each player accurate? Just as in real basketball, where there is some uncertainty about a player's talent level, in Hardwood there is also built-in uncertainty in displayed skill levels. The visible skill values for each player are an approximation of his current actual skill level and may deviate by up to 20% from it true value for some skills. Additionally, just like in real basketball, as a player plays more games, his displayed skill value will approach his true current skill level. Note, this may result in a player's displayed skill level actually dropping, even though he is receiving regular coaching and playing time. His skill value is not actually dropping, but because his actual skill level is better known now, a more accurate and lower value is now displayed." - http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/rules
[2024-11-05 17:09] gards710 : cue the opening of floodgates of people posting 13+ pots with poor dev. my entrants:   http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/169757/A - you could see that his dev in HS was poor for a 13 pot. but the size and the eval blinded me.   http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/160459/A - meh HS dev masked by one really good year  agree with what Naph and cdilks have already posted. Although to address the dev rate v playing time question, they're both factors. Dev rate is not "hidden", but it's not completely tied to potential, nor is it completely tied to playing time. It's not even completely tied to both. There's just an "intrinsic" or "internal" dev rate that players have. Potential might indicate how that might grow and playing time is a modifier that takes that dev rate and produces the actual development. But all 3 are pretty different from each other, although related.

[2025-01-15 19:18] _plokmijn : Depends on potential and starting SI. An average of +10 per season is what I require to consider most prospects. Ideally you want the same dev as potential per year (+44 for 11 POT, +48 for 12 POT, etc).   For prospects with low starting SI, I usually only take ones that are in the +50 range or above since it’s the only way to reach their SI cap in college.   On the other hand, players with high starting SI tend to hit an invisible dev ceiling in HS that makes their dev look worse. Just have to look at the earlier years to project where their college dev might land

[2025-01-17 17:34] eljefe7705 : in general, - if it an "opponent" setting to compensate for a lot of 3's / PITP - you want to set the lower threshold over/equal to a certain amount. E.g., Lower Threshold >= 10, Upper Threshold = none. Conversely, if you are adjusting because you THOUGHT they'd do well for one of those but stunk in the first have then Lower Threshold = none, Upper Threshold <=10 - for point differential - if you want to set something up that (a) triggers within a narrower range (maybe you're losing by a little or winning by a little), Lower Threshold >= -5, Upper Threshold <= 5, (b) triggers when you are losing, LT = none, UT <= -10, (c) triggers when you are winning, LT >=10, UT = none - for your "own" 3's / PITP / Personal Fouls, it would follow a similar methodology whether you're scoring a lot from there (LT >=10) and not as much as you thought (HT <=10)

[2025-01-26 16:42] eljefe7705 : My view on the green light settings are more that you're telling a guy how selective you want him to be vs shoot or not. So an X basically says "you only take it if it's there" which will reduce shot total usually but also will promote more efficiency because he's taking higher percentage shots
[2025-01-26 16:43] eljefe7705 : Also means he will pass more and needs to be smart about picking his spots so it's a multi-attribute consideration
[2025-01-26 16:44] eljefe7705 : That's why you see some guys do better on particular green light settings than others and why some great scorers do better with no green light than ++ for example

[2025-02-08 16:07] zyrok12 : Any advice on what to look for in Assistant Coaches?
[2025-02-08 16:54] flushednevada : Most of the time you're either going to find ACs with 10s across the board, or who have started to show unfavorable comments/development. The approach I hear often is to target young ACs and hope you get one who develops favorably.
[2025-02-08 16:54] zyrok12 : Do ACs actually have an impact?
[2025-02-08 16:57] flushednevada : For the best answer I'd recommend reading the players manual. I believe their impact is minimal, especially relative to the HC, but it does exist. Just hard to quantify. The clearest AC impact I've ever seen is if you replace an AC who is a poor recruiter with one who is a good recruiter you'll get a bump on your recruits.
[2025-02-08 16:58] flushednevada : I try to keep my AC's net positive in terms of their development, and am mostly just fishing for a replacement HC - one of higher quality than I'd be able to just hire from the visible candidates.
[2025-02-08 16:59] flushednevada : Better/more experienced presidents might have a different approach, of course

[2025-03-04 18:16] tcm12 : What's the best way to get more rebounds?  Obviously packing the paint but is zone or man better to grab boards, and are there any other tactics that help?
[2025-03-04 22:23] naph7777 : Man is generally considered better than zone for rebounding.  In general if you’re losing the boards I’d recommend a slower tempo. Try and improve your shot quality as you won’t be getting 2nd chances.
[2025-03-04 22:46] tcm12 : So zone is better than man or man is better than zone?
[2025-03-04 22:58] infinite_tea : He said man is better than man. Are you even listening?
[2025-03-04 22:59] infinite_tea : https://tenor.com/view/dont-you-get-it-kyle-broflovski-butters-stotch-south-park-s14e1-gif-22899432
[2025-03-04 23:41] gards710 : At least in real basketball, man is better specifically for rebounding. But I can’t say if that holds for hw
[2025-03-04 23:50] naph7777 : Sorry, corrected above.
[2025-03-04 23:52] naph7777 : While the generality of Man > Zone for rebounding is true I imagine its dependent on skillsets and situation. If you're playing man, and you have a sluggish 7' monster rebounder who is being dragged out of the key by a stretch-5, and no other plus rebounders on the team.... then you may well be better off with Zone in that situation.
[2025-03-04 23:59] tcm12 : Gotcha.  So man defense Is better for rebounding but zone is better at post defense?
[2025-03-05 00:05] naph7777 : Zone is better at getting your interior players to defend the interior and your perimeter players to defend the perimeter. Steve has shared on the forums that the type of Zone used is PG-SG-SF on the perimeter and PF-C in the paint. Its also generally better for sharing the defensive assignment on a player. For example if your opponent has say a C that is good at drawing fouls, maybe a Zone might be a good idea if you have 2 guys who could defend him, so you share the fouls across your PF & C, instead of almost all of them coming on your C.
[2025-03-05 00:06] squidwardfrommegamind : Oh that's actually a nice bit of information, good to know
[2025-03-05 00:07] naph7777 : Its one of the reasons that PD is a bit more valuable on a SF than ID.
[2025-03-05 00:09] squidwardfrommegamind : So if you have guards who have slightly higher ID then man could be a way to utilize it because they'd maybe be able to defend drivers better
[2025-03-05 00:11] naph7777 : And potentially they are more likely to get switched onto a big, or get posted up by a power-guard etc. They are very unlikely to get posted up against in a Zone.
[2025-03-05 00:13] squidwardfrommegamind : That's interesting to know, thanks
[2025-03-05 00:30] stromstar : ****Is widely considered to be more valuable SFs can still do well the other way around
[2025-03-05 00:33] naph7777 : Sure, but I don't think you'd want to run 90% Zone with a 15/5 ID/PD SF for example.

[2025-03-11 04:14] .julioso : whats the difference between the substitution modes
[2025-03-11 04:35] naph7777 : Substitution Mode: players may be substituted all at once (mass substitution) or in a more distributed manner (staggered substitution).  Listed below are the subsitution options and the typical starter rest intervals. Starters rest is also subject to playing time game management setting  Mass Substitution     All positions: minutes 7-15  Staggered Substitution A (the original)     C: minutes (remaining in the half) 18-11     PG & SF: minutes 15-8     SG & PF: minutes 12-5  Staggered Substitution B (best pattern to have "key" positions filled with optimal players)     PG & C: minutes 18-11     SG & PF: minutes 12-5     SF: minutes 15-8  Staggered Substitution C (shorter bench periods)     C: minutes 18-15 & 12-9     PF: minutes 15-12 & 6-3     SF: minutes 12-6     SG: minutes 18-15 & 6-3     PG: minutes 15-12 & 9-6  - http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/rules  Oh combine with this bit... Note: positions will be filled in the following order: PG, C, PF, SF and SG. So if you have one player as the primary backup for both guard spots - if both starters are on the bench, then the backup player will fill in at PG and the game engine will move to the next position on the depth chart to grab a SG.  between those 2 you can work out who will come in, for each position.
[2025-03-11 17:57] tcm12 : Does it really make that much of a difference which substitution mode you use?  I've just always used A but maybe B is better?  Because unless you're doing mass subs, I don't feel like they'd make that much of a difference
[2025-03-11 17:58] gards710 : not huge differences. small ones tho. mostly has to do with players playing multiple positions
[2025-03-11 18:23] tcm12 : So if I have players playing multiple positions, which would be best?
[2025-03-11 18:28] gards710 : it depends on which positions the player(s) have to cover
[2025-03-11 18:31] tcm12 : http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/depth_chart/430
[2025-03-11 18:31] tcm12 : I didn't know that it mattered if the depth chart was filled with different players or not.  I just figured to put the best SI in
[2025-03-11 18:38] gards710 : you just can't have a player start at two positions. But there is a positional hierarchy in terms of which positions a player who is slotted to play multiple positions will play. So if you have a player who is supposed to be in at SF but then also backs up PG, then bc of positional hierarchy, he'll play PG and then your next SF on the depth chart will come in. and don't just go by pure SI
[2025-03-11 18:53] tcm12 : So I should go by the main ratings for each position instead of just overall SI?  So for PG- Hnd, IQ, Pass; for C- IS, ID, Reb; etc.?

[2025-04-17 20:00] tcm12 : Is it better to run a faster or slower paced offense to prevent turnovers?  I'd assume slower but maybe it's not
[2025-04-17 20:08] flushednevada : Playing slow can reduce total turnovers (because you have fewer possessions) but if your team doesn’t have the right attributes it might not improve TO%. Your team will be passing, dribbling, and generally making more decisions with the ball, so if they’re bad at those things slowing it down may not be the answer
[2025-04-17 20:09] tcm12 : Gotcha.  So if I have bad passing/dribbling/etc. it's probably better just to play at a faster pace?
[2025-04-17 20:17] flushednevada : It could be. There are so many variables, there’s not a one size fits all answer. In my mind you want to maximize the value of your team’s possessions. TOs are one part of that. Shooting % , OR%, etc are other pieces. It’s valuable to think about how these things move in relation to each other.
[2025-04-17 20:53] squidwardfrommegamind : The way I look at it is if your team sucks at passing/dribbling then it could be good to go faster, but if your team happens to also suck at everything else then maybe not so much because you don't really want more possessions in the game
[2025-04-18 02:57] naph7777 : Also tempo is not just team pace setting, but you need to combine it with green light settings. If you ever end up with a lineup where everyone has been told not to shoot at all, then you're going to play slow and end up with shot-clock violations a lot.  Similarly if you set everyone to ++ green light, it won't really matter if you're set to -5 pace, as you're still very likely to take a shot early in the shot clock.
[2025-04-18 02:59] squidwardfrommegamind : I think green lights are the most important thing to keep experimenting with, one slight green light change on one player can totally change what your offense looks like

[2025-05-31 13:43] euphael : Got a couple of questions regarding recruitment process.  1) Is it worth coming after prospects our of my region (not in general just one piece per year for instance)? If I start working on a freshmen could this be the good way? 2) The players evaluation changes every season as well as their stars/potential? 3) At what point you can see in prospect's report information such as he might not academically qualify for college or he does/does not prefer to stay at home?
[2025-05-31 13:45] gards710 : 1) no unless we're talking end of season or you're in the highest league levels 2) the eval can get comments added like poor student or troubled kid, and their star rating is updated, but their potential and the bulk of their eval will not change 3) any point in high school, during the flip (but others claim these comments have popped up during the season)
[2025-05-31 13:46] infinite_tea : 1) As long as they aren’t highly sought after and depending on the region, it’s possible. But do recognize that new recruits generate for every class at the flip, so just because you can’t find someone in your region that you like now, they might generate next season. 2) The evaluation comments stay the same, so does potential. Only stars change. Recruits can get comments about academics, but that’s the only change. 3) These comments appear at flip. Preference for home/not home is less likely to appear after the recruit has been generated, but academic comments can certainly appear.
[2025-05-31 13:47] infinite_tea : For 1, it’s definitely preferred to stay in region as a lower level team.

[2025-06-05 01:39] flushednevada : It's not surprising that the conversations about IQ typically go back to PGs, given the volume of on ball decisions they make. But I wonder if its impact is a lot broader. I like to think that on offense the off ball players benefit from IQ - cutting, spacing, posting up mismatches against zone, etc. And that it would play a similar role on defense, i.e. helping with positioning, help defense, reading the passing lanes etc. And I also wonder if there isn't some sort of scaled aspect it? Having a 20 IQ PG with a low IQ supporting cast might not yield the same benefits as a 13 IQ PG with a high IQ team around him, where they all work in tandem. I'd love to know what El Jefe is learning with his Goldey team, since I think that is at least one of the principles underlying it.

[2025-06-10 15:05] tcm12 : How similar are extended defense and pressure?  I've always thought that a high extended defense (+5) will guard above the three point line while the opposite (-5) is a defense packed inside the paint.  Is that true?  And do we know if extended defense comes into play with pressure defense as well?  For example, if +5 extended pressure defense is a full court pressure, what would a -5 be?  Like a half court trap?  Or does the extended defense only matter if you run man or zone?
[2025-06-10 15:08] flushednevada : I’ve always thought that extension/packing influenced your set defense. I’d imagine that pressure influences the other team inbounding the ball and transitioning down the court. So extension and packing wouldn’t have any impact on that portion of the game. But very interested to hear others thoughts
[2025-06-10 15:08] naph7777 : I think Pressure is separate to defensive extension. Pressure is sending people to trap the ball carriers and try and force turnovers early in the shot-clock. Once the press is beaten, you fall back into whatever Man/Zone/Extension you have set for half-court D.
[2025-06-10 15:09] naph7777 : So you can press.... and then try and run teams off the 3-point line. (+5) or you can press.... and then pack the paint (-5).
[2025-06-10 15:11] tcm12 : Interesting.  Good to know
[2025-06-10 15:11] tcm12 : So is a high extension similar to a press in the sense of you're guarding them higher up, and while you may get burned sometimes, it should in theory force more turnovers?
[2025-06-10 15:14] flushednevada : I think of my extension as impacting shot selection/efficiency more than it does turnovers. Players individual attributes impact the likelihood that they’d force a turnover in either a zone/man and extended/packed defense
[2025-06-10 15:14] flushednevada : If I extend I’m trying to drive my opposition off the three point line or drive the efficiency of the shots they take there down. Packing the paint is the same principle.
[2025-06-10 15:15] naph7777 : Logically, I would think that putting pressure on the perimeter should result in more handling checks and make some passes harder (and probably some passes easier). Buts its hard to get that level of detail out of the text engine that we have.
[2025-06-10 15:16] tcm12 : Ok.  That's what I've always kind of assumed, but I just didn't know how playing a pressure with a -5 defense would play out since I have an undersized team
[2025-06-10 15:32] naph7777 : The best counter-argument is that your Zone + Man + Press can't go above 100. Which seems to indicate that you're either using Pressure, or Man, or Zone.... and the Extend Defense setting doesn't make a lot of sense in combination with Pressure. You can't really play Pressure defense and pack the paint at the same time.
[2025-06-10 15:32] naph7777 : So I suspect that Extend Defense simply only applies to Zone/Man, and is disregarded whenever your team is Pressuring.

[2025-06-30 17:54] spencp99 : You want everyone on your roster to be around that range, outside of specific circumstances. The only players you should really think about when setting playing time is your starting five.
[2025-06-30 17:55] spencp99 : You want everyone in that range (28-35) because then the game will play them more if a starter gets in foul trouble or injured. If you only set exactly 200 minutes of PT across your whole team, everything will fall apart if someone misses a single minute due to fouling out or getting hurt.

[2025-08-15 16:36] naph7777 : Just seems to be a fairly flatly applied penalty to increasing interest on a player. Appears to have some effect on all levels of recruit but is more pronounced on 4 and 5 star prospects.   Its been a long while since I've redshirted a 5-star and its always hard to isolate various recruiting effects. You may have noticed that the cost to increase interest one sublevel can change from season to season. (Number of players at similar position, league level, change of coaches, number of open scholarships etc).
[2025-08-15 16:38] kcb76_58795 : You're the best, thanks.
[2025-08-15 16:38] naph7777 : In the seasons after redshirting Toby Henry, SMC had some targets go from taking 4-6 contacts to increase one sublevel to needing 9-12 per sub level. At the time I was only going after 3-stars and below. Some other guys didn't seem to get effected.

[2025-08-15 16:40] naph7777 : Plenty of others in the Discord have redshirted one or even multiple 5-stars more recently, so they might share too. [2025-09-24 04:04] mdoman12 : My process upon opening a recruits page is as follows:  1. check how tall they’ll be to see if they’d fit what I’m looking for.   2. Check overall SI growth rate to see if it’s meeting the criteria I look for (usually potential x years in school) and then look at the actual current build.   3. Read comments to see if there are any huge red flags (bad shooter/defender/really slow G)  4. Open dev graphs and look for dev in the areas I care about for the position I’m recruiting for.   If they check all those boxes I’m good to go. Usually if a guy isn’t hitting his overall growth rate I’m staying away but I make some exceptions if there’s certain things I really like.
[2025-09-24 04:08] mdoman12 : SI matters but you also need the context for it. There’s nothing wrong with taking a raw recruit as long as you have a plan in place to get him the opportunity he needs to turn into a guy for you. Bigs you can be more lenient with in terms of dev as there are fewer to go around and in some cases guys with really good height/weight/wingspan/vert will be able to make up for having a lower SI. A good example of this is my current True freshman big Robert McWilliams. Believe he’s at 99 SI and hasn’t developed very well overall each of his final two HS years as a 10 pot. BUT he’s 7’1, 270 and has developed well in Rebounding and Interior Defense. So even if he’s not meeting the overall marks that would round him out as a player he’s still developing really well in arguably the two most important categories for a big outside of Inside Shot.
[2025-09-24 04:17] mdoman12 : If you are going after lower SI guys in highschool though, make sure you’re going after guys who are developing at a high level. A low SI 11 pot who’s just hitting +11 SI a year isn’t going to likely be worth it. Look for guys that started low but have gone well above their pot in growth a couple times early in HS say a +30 overall.
[2025-09-24 11:18] bergkamp7349 : ^^That looks about my method, but checking speed is very much in step 1 along with height. Really quick way to discard loads of players.  I probably miss on some players who end up with 10-13 speed or so in college so do need to be a bit careful, but there's so many players out there I'm ok missing on a few.

[2025-11-04 19:26] tcm12 : What's the best way to schedule difficulty?  Do most people just do any?  Or is up or down better?
[2025-11-04 19:32] freewynd : depends on where your team is at.  If you want any shot at an at-large in D1 on the lower levels you probably have to schedule up.  D2 probably doesn't make a huge difference one way.  D3 you probably have to schedule up if you want an at-large.  Of course scheduling up only helps if you can win games.

[2025-11-04 20:37] bergkamp7349 : - if you're bad & not gonna make the tourney either way, I'd schedule down - more winnable games = nice - freewynd covered d3 and d2 well above, if you're a good team wanting to test yourself I'd lean up rather than any.  - a strong team in a top division it probably doesn't matter loads as your in conference schedule will determine RPI, etc more than OOC.  - this is where I start looking at my freshman / redshirters for that season vs my total squad quality & depth. [2025-11-17 01:12] naph7777 : At the very least I
[2025-11-17 01:18] naph7777 : Option 1) Put 1-contact scholarship offers on some guys showing none interest that you can stomach and hope they commit early before others gain interest. Signing 1 or 2 of these guys early will give you more confidence to stay in the H vs H battles. (Pick 1 to focus on, trying to chase 2 at the same time probably means you lose both)  Option 2) Stop putting contacts into the H vs H battles now and try to pivot to a more attainable class now. Maybe you get lucky and win one of the HvsH without more investment. Maybe you don't but you raise the floor of your class by spending contacts on getting decent guys in the clear.  Option 3) Burn all your contacts on the HvsH battles and see where you are once they commit. Maybe the highest ceiling option, but also the lowest floor.  Option 4) Try to get 1 guy at your position of greatest need in the clear (preferably all the way to High).... then battle it out on your top targets.   All of this depends on how much risk you want to take on, just how good the HvsH guys are, what other options you have available etc.

[2025-12-12 00:56] naph7777 : I mean in theory you can play better passers/ball-handlers. You can counter-press to tire both teams out more if you have superior depth. You can try and run faster to provide less ball-handling/passing opportunies for your opponents to turn you over, and to tire them out faster.  But often your best lineup is clearly your best lineup and doing so is counter-productive. Generally I just run what I run and if the press is good enough to beat me, then I tip my hat.
[2025-12-12 00:57] naph7777 : Ticking everyone up a bit in green-light can also help with reducing turnover opportunities. But increasing tempo and green-light settings overall tends to result in funnelling more shots to your backcourt and that's not always something you want to do either.

[2025-12-16 10:03] adrian_toth : https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/roster/402 What should I do with Bridgeport? I have 3 starters who should be really good shooters on paper and my bigs shouldn't be bad at inside scoring either but still no matter what I try the team finds a way to suck
[2025-12-16 12:35] naph7777 : You’re getting beat up on the boards and don’t have a lot of passing/handling.  I’d slow the tempo a bit. -2 or -3 maybe, but that might be too slow for your passing? Probably needs a lower green light on your PG for the slower tempo, then with a bunch of guys on + green light. You want your PG to take his time to make the right pass, but then the shot to go up reasonably quickly. ++ only for guys with a favourable matchup.   Use I, i and ~ team offensive focus more often so that your bigs get more looks and can suck the defense in to open up the outside for your shooters, or simply make them pay if they are hugging your guys on the perimeter. In the 2nd half of you’re losing maybe up to 0 tempo and flip your strategy to either I or O depending on the matchup and what you did in the first half.    I’d probably drop Kennedy back to “o” (I assume he’s “O” at the moment) just to mix up his offense a bit.   Defensively you have to decide if you’re going to cover your PF problem or accept them and cover other places you are stronger instead. Again you may want to mix that up a bit. Sometimes you have a weakness you can’t cover and accepting it is the better option.

[2025-12-28 08:33] rojo6176 : I am quite new and I don't get what penalty do you mean? If you red shirt a lot of players you will have a penalty? Am I right ?  What kind of penalty ?
[2025-12-28 09:53] stromstar : When you redshirt a player, recruits will be less likely to develop interest in your school because immediate playing time is one of the interest factors.    That means that the year after you redshirt a player, you might need to spend more contacts to progress the interest level of a recruit. A penalty of sorts.  Redshirting a 1-star is such a negligible penalty you likely won't notice it. In fact, redshirting a 3-star regarded to be small enough that the meta strategy has become one in which most teams just redshirt everyone. There have been multiple posts that say the 4-star redshirt penalty is worth taking, but whether it's worth redshirting 5-stars is where the great debate lies.
[2025-12-28 09:54] stromstar : Oh, and these penalties gradually wear off over time as the players age your reputation clears up.
[2025-12-28 10:02] rojo6176 : Ok thanks for the answer, that might explain why almost no one wants to come to my team (I have redshirted everyone who came in my team last year). But it was mostly 2 or 3 stars, so shouldn't be a big penalty, or it's the accumulation of 2 and 3 that made a penalty or maybe just bad luck ^^
[2025-12-28 11:30] stromstar : Lots of things affect recruiting. In no particular order here's the factors that I can think of:  Coach recruiting abilities Firing coaches Recruit's star rating Coach contact points Contact timing Conference level Prestige Location Quality of roster Age of roster Redshirting players Random factors

[2026-01-05 15:01] kbenny139979 : when is the best time to snag a new head coach? I usually just spam hire young assistants until I find one with good traits but I'm running out of time.
[2026-01-05 15:06] naph7777 : First week after the flip is generally the best time to look.   Coaches when they are released get a randomised length of delay before they become avilable again. That delay seems to extend up to a few days (I'm not sure exactly how long). As bot head coaches (and assistants) are often released at the flip this is when the greatest number of head coaches appear over the course of the season.

[2026-01-05 15:51] naph7777 : His range from his eval comments is... Offense: 11-13   Development: 11 Defense: 0-6    Motivation: 9-11 approx, probably stay at 10 Tactics: 12-15   Recruiting: 15+   That said, given how long you've had him I wouldn't expect any of the attributes to really move more than 1 more than where they are  So best case:  12 - 12  6 - 11 13 - 15  Worse case: 11 - 11  5 - 9 12 - 15  So he's slightly above average to barely above average. But if the areas he's good at is what you value, then you've got a HC for the next 23 seasons, and long term stability is worth something too.  Can you get better? Maybe. Can you get better that is younger? Probably not. So it kinda depends on how often you want to go through the pain of a HC change versus how much you want a better HC.

[2026-01-13 11:22] fireballer34 : How do you guys decide how much offensive pace to have, or how much zone to run?
[2026-01-13 11:36] bengalman : vibes
[2026-01-13 12:51] flushednevada : If my team is good at creating a possession advantage vs other teams by winning the TO battle and/or winning on the boards then I am typically going to play faster. Creates more possessions over which you can assert that advantage, and you can turn steals into fast break offense, which is generally very efficient.   Same case can be made for if your team reliably shoots it better than opponents. The advice generally boils down to “if you’re better, play faster”.  Pace has other applications, like if your team has a high TO% you can crank the pace to get faster shots. The idea being that you’ll spend less time in halfcourt passing it, which means fewer chances for errant passes etc. I’ve also heard of pace being used to counter high pressure opponents, but can’t speak to that too much.
[2026-01-13 12:54] flushednevada : Over time I’ve played faster and faster. I don’t know many managers who play slow. Maybe <@607683593686352012> still does, if memory serves MMA played -5 pace at one point.
[2026-01-13 13:15] flushednevada : As far as zone and man are concerned, I typically experiment with different splits till I find what works.   At the highest level, I believe it is generally agreed that zone better defends the 2 and man better defends the 3. Additionally, man is going to help you keep specific matchups between you and your opponent’s players/postions, whereas zone will result in switching.   Typically find a baseline for my team and then adjust it based on the information above.
[2026-01-13 13:26] naph7777 : * players who flourish/struggle at various paces effect my pace (care way more about starters than bench guys) From here down is relative to my opponent(s) * more depth = faster * higher stamina = faster * Rebound advantage = faster * Turnover advantage = faster * eFG% advantage = faster * bad team handles/passing pushes towards 0 pace (too fast and too slow can both lead to more turnovers) * run offense through guards = faster * run offense through bigs = slower * I also tend to run slower if I have good overall IQ/Passing as I trust that team to make the extra pass and find the best shot. But you see high IQ/Passing teams do just fine playing fast too. * I suspect a high finishing team would also do better running fast, but I don’t know if I’ve ever had one that was good enough to be the deciding factor.
[2026-01-13 13:39] squidwardfrommegamind : I usually go fast when I have a lot of shooting with not so much dribbling (Often) so that they don't try to pass it around a lot and turn it over all the time
[2026-01-13 13:41] flushednevada : I forget the impact that pace has on shot distribution throughout the different positions
[2026-01-13 13:52] eljefe7705 : Opponent capabilities should also pay a role in your pace settings and adjustments. If someone is inside heavy, i never go too slow and then if they're scoring inside I'll adjust to play faster
[2026-01-13 13:54] eljefe7705 : Last year against Ripon and Xavier, I knew I was overmatched and couldn't keep up with their shooting, so I played a lot slower than normal
[2026-01-13 14:16] naph7777 : ECU played at negative speed in most games last year for at least a half.  Western Michigan and Central Arkansas both played really slow last year.
[2026-01-13 14:21] naph7777 : Another advantage of Zone that I don’t see posted in here often is sharing fouls around.   If your opponent has a guy that gets to the line a lot, it can be helpful to have multiple guys defending them (via a zone) so that you aren’t as likely to get a starter in foul trouble as quickly.
[2026-01-13 14:45] flushednevada : I understand that this can be very team specific, but generally where is too slow and too fast on the pace range for you? Or would you conceivably  move all the way from -5 to +5 with the same team?  Understanding if an adjustment is “too extreme” is still a sense I’m developing.
[2026-01-13 14:47] naph7777 : I tend to operate in the +3 to -3 range most often.  Worth noting that green light settings also affects your overall tempo and results in you playing faster or slower.
[2026-01-13 14:48] naph7777 : I should probably experiment more with the extremes. It’s been a while since I have.
[2026-01-13 14:50] naph7777 : Too slow is when you start noticing shot-clock violations, and/or lots of possessions are passed around a lot until there is a turnover or too high a percentage of your shots are beating the shot clock rather than being a “good shot”
[2026-01-13 14:52] naph7777 : Too fast is when you see guys throwing the ball away early in the shot-clock too much, or when the pace messes with your shot distribution too much. (Scoring bigs don’t get enough touches, guards who aren’t meant to shoot much are leading your team in FGA etc)
[2026-01-13 17:20] cdilks : I think one of the big considerations for man vs. zone is the overall athleticism of your team/opponent. Zone will keep a slow defender from getting blown by as often, but is more susceptible to hot shooting, espeically outside. Man is more effective if you've got guys fast/quick enough to stay in front of their opponent, but is also more susceptible to fouling.

[2026-01-19 00:50] cadions : 1. The projected height can update as recruits age but sometimes it under or over projects how tall they will be so it isn't always the most accurate. A good rule of thumb is add like 7 or 8 inches to the recruits height their freshman year of hs and that gives you a rough idea where you can expect them.
[2026-01-19 00:52] cadions : 2. Physicals are quite important for defense, especially stuff like speed and strength and to a lesser extend vertical. For example, I have a player with 5 PD but like 16 speed and decent strength and they are a pretty good perimeter defender at D3 at least. I look at them roughly equally though between physicals and defense tho but thats just me
[2026-01-19 00:54] naph7777 : 2. Lots of factors. Physical measurements is certainly part of it. Evaluation comments, rate of progression in HS. ID/PD split relative to height/position. worth noting that a seemingly negative comment (will never be a good interior/perimeter defender) is a positive for the right position, especially if paired with the good all-around defender comment. Spd, Str and probably IQ can all help some too.
[2026-01-19 00:55] naph7777 : Projected height is a lie. Just add 7.5”, and you’ll usually be right an sometimes be happy that they grew 8” instead.

[2026-01-21 15:33] naph7777 : From the [rules](https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/rules):  Game Tactics: how well does the coach construct game tactics that counter his opponent and highlight his teams strengths, particularly at the end of games.  Motivation: how well can the coach motivate the team such that and control and cope with swings in game momentum.  From my opinion: Tactics: I take this to mean things like, you set your team team at say 0 extension, but as the half goes on your coach notices that the other team is pounding the ball into the post on most possessions and he can make the change on the fly to bring the defense in some. Similarly your opponent is packing the paint, so he runs a few more plays to spring a shooter open on the outside. The higher the tactics, the sooner the coach can react to opponent focuses and weaknesses within each half.  Motivation: A higher motivation coach is more likely to go on big runs and mitigate opponent runs. No lead is safe for a low motivation coach and they rarely will mount large comebacks.

[2026-01-23 03:31] ogmayo10 : Interesting

[2026-01-23 03:31] naph7777 : You probably shouldn't play the team you are going to blow out the same way you are going to play the team that probably blows you out.

[2026-01-23 06:31] .julioso : is there anything specific you look at when making adjustments?
[2026-01-23 06:50] naph7777 : Does my opponent have relevant injuries? Who is likely to start if so?  Do I think I will win or lose the possession game?  Where does my opponent take most of their FG from (range and position)?  Which position(s) is my opponents weakest at defending?  Is my opponent better at defending 2’s or 3’s?  Does my opponent shoot many 3’s?  Do any of my opponents draw a lot of fouls? Are they foul prone?  How much passing/handling does my opponent have?  How much does my opponent press? Have they been vulnerable to pressing teams?  Later in the season, how have other teams beaten this opponent? How did the first game against them go? Has their starters/rotation changed?
[2026-01-23 06:55] naph7777 : That sounds like a lot, but if you open an opponent’s roster, depth chart and stats (conference only once they’ve played a few) and schedule in different tabs, you can answer most of those questions pretty quickly.   Schedule is more of deep dive for key games.  If a player is injured I might look at their game logs to see who started instead of them if they were injured previously.
[2026-01-23 09:39] .julioso : would you increase your pace if you feel as if your going to lose the possession game?   which numbers do you look at to determine if a team is defending 2’s or 3’s?
[2026-01-23 11:10] naph7777 : I'd decrease the pace if I was going to lose out on possessions. (Your hope of winning is to be more efficient on less shots. The more shots in the game, the less chance you have of that happening)  On PC if you mouseover the FG% value for their opponents it shows 2P%, 3P% and overall eFG%. Multiple 2P% x 2 and 3P% x3 and you have a rough guide as to what they defend comparatively better/worse. (You should factor 2P% slightly higher as you get more FTA from 2FGA)
[2026-01-23 19:13] ogmayo10 : THE STINK CONTINUES
[2026-01-23 19:14] ogmayo10 : GET THAT 3% BELOW 20% BABY
[2026-01-24 07:04] .julioso : what would you change if a team draws a lot of fouls or if they commit a lot of fouls?  when you look at handling/passing of the opponent does that effect how much pressure you use?   Im assuming the FG range and position affects the extension  and what ever position their weakest defender is at you increase the green light at  that position on your team
[2026-01-24 08:36] naph7777 : If they have a player that draws a lot of fouls I might play more zone (shares fouls across multiple positions), or I might consider which of my bigs I can most afford to foul out for example. If my team doesn’t have depth at that position I might consider lower pressure and/or lower tempo. (Less possessions in the game and more time in offence is less opportunities to foul)  Handling/passing is for pressure yes.  Yes for range/extension.  Might be green light settings (might even go down against a very good defender). If I have players who can play multiple positions it might also determine matchups.

I personally feel like a 18 SPD 6 PD player would be a better perimeter defender than a 20 PD 5 SPD player

[2026-02-21 02:49] eman38291 : Ok this is genuinely a stupid question but teams on the bubble don’t make it because of conference winners for the tournament right?

[2026-02-21 02:59] gards710 : but there's not usually 16 surprise conference tournament winners, so some will make it
[2026-02-21 03:16] naph7777 : There are 15 auto-bids in D1, one for each conference. Teams "on the bubble" are those that are close to cut-off for "at large" teams that will get in without an auto-bid.  So the answer to your question kind of depends on how you look at it. Do they miss out because a team outside the top 68 won an auto-bid? Or did they miss out because they weren't in the top X non auto-bids?
[2026-02-21 03:24] gards710 : so what you're saying is that there's NEVER 16 surprise conference tourney winners (in D1)
[2026-02-21 03:27] naph7777 : That would be hard with only 15 D1 conferences 😛

[2026-03-04 13:36] freewynd : Weird question, not sure if it's been asked over the years.  If you have an average POT shooting guards with negative comments such as bad rebounding, will that help improve the chances that the pot skills goes to more preferable ones or does it just means that player is less likely to reach max potential?
[2026-03-04 14:44] naph7777 : The short answer is yes. Less rebounding = more of something else.  I think Potential is a reflection of a player’s maximum SI. So a 10-pot with great rebounding will fall in the same range of total  SI (assuming they have the time to reach it) as a never rebounder. To reach the same SI, those points of SI must go into something else.
[2026-03-04 14:47] freewynd : That's what I figured, wasn't 100 percent though, thanks for clarifying.
[2026-03-04 14:51] naph7777 : That's probably too certain of an answer as its pretty hard to actually prove. But I haven't had anything come along that thoroughly disproves it and when you're looking for it, it seems to bear out. Easiest way is to browse through top players. There you can find a bunch of maxed out 12-pots. All with very similar SI. Some with negative comments, some without etc.

[2026-03-21 01:43] swarm4 : I’m new, is there a specific team I should register for that y’all know about?
[2026-03-21 02:02] naph7777 : Generally its less of a learning curve if you just take a team at the bottom. But the disadvantage is that your team is very likely to suck and in game tactics will be close to irrelvant for quite a while.  The alternative is to look for a team that was well managed but only recently has gone idle. Its still likely that you drop down before you plateau or go back up, but it can both be easier for recruiting, and you'll probably have some better pieces to make the games themselves more interesting.
[2026-03-21 02:04] naph7777 : The other thing to consider is the size of the recruiting region for each team. A smaller region will have less competition from other managers, but also less options to recruit, which can mean that you have to learn how to recruit out of region quicker.  I suspect going in a large recruiting area has a higher floor for recruiting. Regardless, they are different types of challenges, so it depends on what you'd rather do.
[2026-03-21 02:05] cadions : I will add on to this - it could be good to go through and look at states you may be interested in and see how many active managers the teams have. [2026-03-21 03:55] naph7777 : __Recruiting Contacts__ You get 29 at the start of each season (AKA the flip), then gain 2 each day (except the last) during the season. Can carry some over from past season's. (any above 10 get cut in half, so its pretty common to carry 10 over and have 39 after the flip.  That works out to having 130 each season. You can only have a max of 45 banked at one time.  They are used for increasing interest on recruits. It will take somewhere between 2-7 contacts to reach Low interest on an in region prospect. It can take 10-15, even more to raise a sub level of interest on out of region, or International recruits.  The levels of interest are Low, Medium, High. Each level has sublevels (Low+, Low++). Sublevels can be seen on your own recruiting board, but not on the recruiting board of other teams. After High++ is "Very High" (which again appears on your board, but not on other people's). You can still gain interest past Very High. Generally you can multiply the number of contacts it took to get to Low to work out how many contacts it will take to reach Medium/High Interest (x4 for Medium, x7 for High), but it often takes a little more than that. There also seems to be some sort of soft cap on how many contacts you can spend on younger players before they stop gaining interest. This seems to be around 20 contacts per year of HS experience. (20 for FR, 40 for SO), its not clear whether points above that soft cap give full value or not when re-evaluated at a flip. Any recruit with at least 1 contact and a scholarship offer can commit to you during the season. (HS SR's start committing on day 5, JuCo's on day 10, INTL's on day 15) - If you're a full level of interest behind someone else they are strongly favored. The effectiveness of each contact is effected by things like: Your team's conference/league-level. Your team's prestige. Your head coach's recruiting skill, assistant coach's skill, redshirts, other talent on the team at same position etc.

[2026-03-27 19:01] swarm4 : • Does setting the game tactics to an inside/outside emphasis take priority over what you set do players in the game management tab?
[2026-03-27 19:02] swarm4 : • Also, zone vs pressure vs extent amounts? If it’s dependent on a team, what should I look for to differentiate?
[2026-03-27 19:02] tcm12 : The faster you play, the more tired your players will get.  Likewise, defense and extension also can fatigue players.  The more extended a defense, the more exhausting it'll be.  Pressure is the most tiring defense, then man, then zone (which is a 3-2 zone).  I would say start all your starters' minutes with 20 + their stamina stat then adjust accordingly.  If they have no fatigue, you can give them another minute or two.  If they have moderate or heavy fatigue, dial it back
[2026-03-27 19:03] tcm12 : Can we get this pinned?
[2026-03-27 19:07] tcm12 : No, team emphasis shows where you will try to get the ball the most.  If you're set on "I" then you're team will try to get an inside.  If "O" then you'll mainly keep it on the perimeter.  Indidivudal emphasis is where the player is.  So guards are naturally gonna be on the outside and bigs on the inside.  If you set a guard on "I" then he will try to drive a lot.  If you set a big to "O" then they'll hang around the outside a little more.  If you set a guard to "O" they'll mainly stay on the outside.  If you set a big to "I" then he will always hang around the paint.  Reading the game manual will help with some of this just fyi
[2026-03-27 19:10] swarm4 : I have the game manual tab open. Nowhere does it specify priority
[2026-03-27 19:10] swarm4 : I'm also trying to ask questions that have more of a "I've been playing this game for X time so here's what I've found works" type answer

[2026-03-27 19:12] tcm12 : Zone is better if you have low speed, a lot of height, or if your guys really high of one defensive stat but really low of the other.    Pressure is good if you have good defense and speed.  It's good to extend your defense if the opposing team is really good at shooting 3s and for packing the paint if they've got dangerous bigs.  Likewise, some people extend the defense if they have really good defensive bigs to dare the opposition to try to shoot on them

[2026-03-27 19:15] tcm12 : Team inside emphasis doesn't mean your team won't shoot 3s, and team outside emphasis doesn't mean you'll only shoot 3s.  Team emphasis is more where you will have the ball the most.  Individual positioning matters more about where that player will be positioned.  If you wanna run 5 out and chuck up 3s, you have to set the team emphasis to "O" and all the individual positionings to "O".  Even then, you'll probably still take some 2s.  If you don't wanna take any 3s, set the team emphasis to "I" and all the individual positionings to "I".

[2026-04-09 00:54] gards710 : different philosophies. Most of us want to have at least one future HC as an AC, but it also depends on timing and amplitude. Will they be a better HC than the current HC or another AC by the time they need to be promoted (or rather, by the time the incumbent needs to be replaced)

Nothing wrong with asking for help, I was simply pointing out what I felt was a contradiction.   I personally get frustrated with seeing specific questions (and answers) about tactics because seriously, no one knows much about tactics in this game. You have to find what works for you and your team. You can try to find teams that play similarly and play like them, or have teams built similarly, and that might help. But there are so many other variables that make copying tactics (or tactical advice) really difficult. From league level to personnel to coaches to little levers in Game Management, to think it will all just go smoothly simply because you took the advice of someone else who might be more successful than you, I think is the wrong path to take

[2026-05-10 14:29] naph7777 : __General Tips__ * Redshirting 3-and-under star players will enable to get the best out of your players. * Evening out your scholarship schedule will prevent you yo-yoing between divisions. Currently have 4 SR's graduating and 3-6 JR's graduating next year. Might want to redshirt 2-3 of the JR's. Waller and Street are good candidates. Redshirting Schneider might hurt your big man rotation this year too much. On the other hand if he does redshirt he probably starts the next 2 years, which might be better. * Rng tends to work better with OS. That said, you can just have guys set to "O" and still get okay'ish eFG if they shoot (and make) enough 3's. They're just even more susceptible to cold spells than a volume 3-point shooter who has OS. * Last season you were a really low turnover team. Hopefully that's a strength again. * Your team is built to go slow, space the floor, move the ball around and hit Burgess on the inside, or find the open shooter on the perimeter. Molina can also attack a close-out and finish or kick on drives.  * A low possession game hopefully helps you reduce the harm on the likely negative rebounding margin, and with a presumably high 3FGA strategy you'll up the variance and be able to steal some games you might otherwise lose. * You should be pretty good defensively, particularly on the perimeter. But the ratings are a little soft on the interior, and combined with the size (particularly when either Burgess or Coppola are off) is going to be problematic. You could mitigate this by playing Schneider this year.

[2026-05-12 03:43] lassoball : My personal rule for foul hook is that if the starter has substantially better production than the backup, I’ll usually give the starter a slow hook to work their way out of early struggles. For production, I’ll primarily look at a player’s eFG vs eOFG when comparing how much the backup is a liability vs. the starter.

[2026-05-12 09:03] stromstar : Yes, no, yes
[2026-05-12 09:11] stromstar : There's 240 D1 teams, 256 D2 teams, and 512 D3 teams. Each conference has 16 teams. D1 has 15 conferences in 4 tiers. The top conference is often referred to as "Legends". Here's the pyramid scheme of conferences.  1 in LL1 (I.1) 2 in LL2 (II.1, II.2) 4 in LL3 (III.1, III.2, III.3, III.4) 8 in LL4 (IV.1, IV.1, IV.3, IV.4, IV.5, IV.6, IV.7, IV.8) ----------------- 16 conferences in 1 tier for D2 (V.1 - V.16) ----------------- 32 conferences in 1 tier for D3 (VI.1 - VI.32)

[2026-05-29 13:55] abefromanthesausagekingofchicago : Good use of AI that I’m going to toss out here for everyone. <@507751197139140609> and I have always conflicted on the impact of pace and fatigue. I’ve generally run a 20+stamina and +2 or +3 pace for Ferrum. When I have a slower lineup running 0 or +1 I go with 22+Sta. Usually have a couple guys on Light/Med fatigue and maybe get the low defensive energy comment but impact seemed minimal and I liked having my starters out there.   This year with early season blowouts it was more noticeable to me that the last quarter of games seemed to cut my PD. I loaded about 15 games or so where I knew I ran +3 and 20+Sta into ChatGPT and the analysis was pretty clear: my offensive output stayed about the same, 10% drop from Q3 to Q4, but my opponents saw about a 39% increase in scoring in Q4 vs Q1! Keep in mind I was forcing opponents  > 1 DQ per game too. As soon as I went to 18+Sta I saw an immediate righting of the ship and have seen Q4 decreases for my opponents   TL;DR if you’re seeing any fatigue on your guys at the end of the game you are probably getting worse performance out of them then you realize!

[2026-06-24 11:50] .julioso : how many contacts do we get after they get halfed at the flip
[2026-06-24 12:34] tcm12 : Depends.  Every point above 10 gets cut in half.  So if you had 20, then you'll have 15 (10 plus the extra 10÷2).  If you have 40, then you'll get 25 (10 + 30÷2)
[2026-06-24 12:36] tcm12 : And then you get 28 at the flip, so if you wanted to have the 45 max at the flip, you'd need to save up 24 (10 + 14÷2 + 28 = 45).  That'd be so you don't waste any unnecessarily

[2026-07-18 01:32] branhd12 : Look at the game logs and you'll see that a lot of fast break opportunities come from live-ball turnovers ("x steals the pass from y", "x turns the ball over to the other team"). Knowing this, the best way to prevent transition is to have players, 1-5, who have IQ and Passing.

[2026-07-18 02:32] naph7777 : Slower tempo means more passes per shot attempt, which makes for more opportunities for turnovers each possession. Upping your green light settings, on the thought that a missed shot is better than a turnover is the only thing that really works I think.

[2026-08-08 02:13] lharm : What's the difference between outside shot and range?
[2026-08-08 02:14] tony9955. : OS = Helps with free throws, making shots from mid-range to threes Range = How far you can take that mid-range and if you can go to the three point line
[2026-08-08 02:14] mdoman12 : Outside Shot (OS): outside jump shooting, required to make shots from mid-range to long distances. Also, instrumental in making free throws.  Range (Rng): ability to make shots from long distances with a high shooting percentage
[2026-08-08 02:16] lharm : I read the rules, they just sound like they say the same thing
[2026-08-08 02:16] mdoman12 : I’ve always viewed it as higher range= better percentage
[2026-08-08 02:17] mdoman12 : On more volume
[2026-08-08 02:17] branhd12 : OS helps with midrange and free throws  3PTS = OS + Range
[2026-08-08 02:17] mdoman12 : So a guy with High os/low range could shoot 33% on 6 3pt attempts, High OS/ High range could shoot 40% on 6 attempts.   Low OS/high range is probably a guy you want 2-4 attempts from at most but he probably shoots 36% or so
[2026-08-08 02:28] tcm12 : The lower the range, the more the shooting percentage will drop off as you get farther from the hoop.  For example, a player with 20 OS and 1 RNG will probably be a mid range deadeye but won't hit many 3s.  On the other hand, someone with 8 OS and 20 RNG won't have the best shooting percentage in the mid range, but his shooting percentage will probably be the same on middies as they are on 3s.  OS is vital for a guard to be able to shoot, but it's unlikely you'll be able to hit many 3s without pairing it with RNG.  Does that help?

[2026-08-18 02:33] creekcat11 : I tend to think of it as the team offensive focus is where is the ball likely to go on scoring attempts. Individual player positioning is where you want them to mostly be on the offensive end. If the team focus is i/I for example, you wouldn't get each individual player plowing into the paint unless you also put them all individually on i or I, which would be dumb because it would crowd the lane and on any rebound you could get burned on a fast break
[2026-08-18 02:33] creekcat11 : So even with a team at i/I, you would want guys on neutral or o/O to draw the defense out and because inside is not their strength.
[2026-08-18 02:35] creekcat11 : Defense might also adjust to move inside and leave any guys at o/O open for longer distance shots. So individual position and team focus have to kind of complement each other but not be the same, depends on the player and what you want them to do in that offensive scheme

[2026-08-26 01:41] maxsmos3 : Can someone explain to me how i lost as badly as i did in my exhibition game today. Although he is d1 i had the better TPI and don’t understand how i lost by 43 points. And if that, what should i change about my future recruiting, etc?
[2026-08-26 02:22] cdilks : They've got some great offensive bigs and had an outlier good 3-pt shooting game. I wouldn't worry too much about the game.
[2026-08-26 02:33] naph7777 : __Tactics__  Your opponent appears to have correctly extended out their defense and your team attempted 37 threes against what looks like +4 or +5 extension for most of the game. Your bigs hardly got any looks, which enabled them to stay locked on your guards.  Your defense started at +1, which is fairly balanced. It was sucked in by the bigs in the first half (getting down to -2.5), then in the second half it got extended out to +3, so they probably hit more 3's in the 2nd half, but that wouldn't have helped defending their bigs either.  __Player Builds__ Your opponent has several more high end ratings than your team does. For example their bigs had 16 & 17 IS going against your 13 & 8 ID and Gilliam had 3 or more inches of height on anyone that defended him. As your defense was also extended out a little, they wouldn't have had much help on the inside. Their perimeter trio have OS/Rng ratings of 15/12, 14/16, 14/7, with 12/14 getting 26 minutes off the bench. Your perimeter guys have 11/12, 13/13, 11/14 with 12/7 the highest minutes guy off the bench.  You do have slightly nicer PD, but those extra points between 11 and 14-16 on the offensive skills matter.  They also had a 7-footer with 15 ID, and their shorter 6' 7½" PF still has a 7' 4¼" wingspan and a 38½" vert so he had a good game defensively for his ID rating as he got 3 blocks as well. You don't have that let of rim protection on your team.  __TPI/WSI__ Although you have higher TPI, they had a higher WSI, which means that of the guys that played minutes they had higher SI.   __Summary__ Their dual inside-outside threat appears to have been far more successful at giving your defense problems, than your outside focussed attack did theirs. I think you probably would have been better off picking either +/-3 or +/-4) to try and take something away rather than try and cover both.
[2026-08-26 02:47] naph7777 : In summary, unless you're markedly better defensively all around, I think you're better off trying to take something away instead of trying to cover everything.  In recruiting, you've got lots of guys who are above average at lots of things, but not really elite at much. All SI isn't equal. I'd far rather have 1 guy with 15 OS and another guy with 5 OS, than 2 guys with 10 OS. Similarly I'd rather have a guy with 15 IS/Fin and 5 OS/Rng (or vice versa), than a guy with all 10's. So you may want to try and acquire guys with more of the top end comments (Vg/dominating post, excellent shooter, really long-range shooter, monster rebounder, great all-around defender, or good all-around + never ID/PD comments). A guy like Turk is definitely a step in the right direction, he's not there yet, but he should become an absolute star for you in the future. Brady might get there with his Spd/Shooting this year, but he's running out of time to fulfil his evaluation.

[2021-11-17 18:01] pschwartz : Ok - here is Coach of the Year.  I wanted to explain some of these numbers though.  Everything is as of the end of the conference playoffs (usually end of year awards don't include postseason but I didn't think of this idea until after).  There are 3 main numbers - TPI, RPI, and PDiff.  The number in parentheses is their rank in all of Division 1 (out of 240 teams).  The number after their conference is their place in the conference.  So Macalaster finished 4th in IV.6, their TPI was 207th, RPI was 17th, and PDiff was 32nd.  PDiff is essentially the percentage they outscore their opponents (so Macalaster on average outscored their opponent by 18% per game).  Hope that makes sense.  I threw Average Height from the depth chart for comparison purposes.  A - Macalester (IV.6, 4th), http://www.onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/845 TPI 137.8 (207), RPI .592 (17), PDiff 18% (32), Avg Height 6’7 B - Lewis & Clark (I.1, 1st), http://www.onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/769 TPI 161.5 (6), RPI .598 (11), PDiff 21% (20), Avg Height 6’7 C - Dominican University of California (I.1, 3rd) http://www.onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/564 TPI 154.2 (44), RPI .576 (38), PDiff 18.3%, Avg Height 6’8 D - Tennessee (I.1, 4th) http://www.onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/64 TPI 153.8 (48), RPI .585 (27), PDiff 15.5% (52), Avg Height 6’6 E - Saint Leo (III.2, 3rd) http://www.onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/642 TPI 146.5 (140), RPI .601 (7), PDiff 15.7% (48), Avg Height 6’6.5 F - Sioux Falls (III.1, 2nd) http://www.onlinecollegebasketball.org/team/553 TPI 149.5 (105), RPI .595 (16), PDiff 24.2% (12), Avg Height 6’6.5

[2023-01-07 18:05] slickandjakenillinois : I thought it was simple but I changed it quite a few times and now it is more complicated.    Basically it is a formula where a team’s score consists of about 30% from SOS, 40% from its WP, 25% from its TPI relative to the highest TPI in the game, and 5% from prestige relative to the highest prestige in the game.  The prestige part tends to give “better” managers a little boost, meaning they may on average overachieve with their talent versus an average manager.

[2024-01-06 01:29] pschwartz : I used to pull the data from conference stats pages but the problem was if a PG had 19/9 the 9 assists would show up but not necessarily the 19 ppg if that wasn't top 10 - so a lot of manual work had to be done to fill in some of that data by hand.
[2024-01-06 01:30] pschwartz : Now I just pull in the top 10 players for each of the top 120 RPI teams from the team's individual statistics pages - so now I have every data point
[2024-01-06 01:32] pschwartz : I can figure out who are the PGs by ranking each player by assists for their individual team - player with the most assists is most likely the PG.  The top 2 players in rebounding are your PF/C.  #3 in rebounding is your SF and whoever is left is your SG.  Before I really have no idea who was what position, but now I can probably get it 90% correct by just doing some excel stuff.

[2024-04-25 11:56] poletz : So this is my contribute. I like this voting game and I don't want to be a party pooper. However, for some time I have been thinking about a way to extract the data in a complete way and find a more analytical way possible to elect the best player(s) for each role. Maybe I finally did it. I'm sharing it with you to get your opinion on the matter. Feel free to ask if anything is unclear. essentially I take into consideration the true shooting%, the ofg (inverted so as to reward the defender's skill), and the sum of the bonus malus of the match (excluding what concerns the points since there is already true shooting). those last are adjusted by team possession and minutes played. In the table I show the percentile in which they are positioned (among their equal roles) for each of these categories. the top 15 ranking is made up of the teams that have the best overall score in the 3 categories described above. the other statistics are just to give more detail but do not contribute to the ranking. The pool is all players with PG as main role that played at least 600 total min in D1 conference games. only conf stats are considered.
[2024-04-25 11:58] poletz : Nice to see that the players that got voted in the poll are in the list (7th and 13th).. i feel Golden is actually the one that deserves it more btw
[2024-04-25 13:54] naph7777 : A few columns I'm not sure of. FP? - what is this? Adj. Bonus? - how is this calculated? Inv OFG - is this just changed so that higher is better? adj. Eff - how is this calculated? A-T = Assists minus Turnovers?
[2024-04-25 14:02] poletz : Final position (conf. Standings) please suggest a better name 🙂 Adjusted bonus: (A+R+S+B-T-PF+FD)/min played/team poss x32 x80. Inv ofg yes (it s 100-ofg ) 👍 Adj eff : (P+A+R+S+B-T-PF+FD-missedFG-missedFTA)/min played /team pos x 32 x 80. Assist-turnovers , right 👍

[2024-04-25 14:47] naph7777 : Game Score is PTS + 0.4 * FG - 0.7 * FGA - 0.4*(FTA - FT) + 0.7 * ORB + 0.3 * DRB + STL + 0.7 * AST + 0.7 * BLK - 0.4 * PF - TOV Even though it was designed for a single game, you can do it across a season's stats for a rough "everything in one number" kind of stat. There seems to be a general consensus that it values scoring too much though.
